To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conditional bias correction method is effective in correcting the deficiencies of naive EB confidence intervals.

(i) in the non-exchangeable case, the naive intervals are generally too short and do not attain the nominal coverage probability; and (ii) in the exchangeable case the naive intervals are too short, do not attain the coverage probability, and do not provide a statement of conditional calibration.

(1) the conditional bias correction method is a useful approach to developing empirical Bayes confidence intervals, (2) the method can be applied to a wide range of problems, and (3) it is a useful tool for developing EB methods in general.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of EB confidence intervals in a nonexchangeable parametric setting.
the problem of obtaining confidence intervals for the parameter of interest in a parametric empirical Bayesian model.
the construction of empirical Bayes confidence intervals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the EM interval is the preferred interval for empirical Bayes confidence intervals, with the exception that in the case of the normal mean with a noninformative prior, the EB interval has better coverage than the EM interval.
the EM intervals are more accurate than the naive EB intervals, and the EM intervals have better properties than the naive EB confidence intervals.
the EM method is an excellent approach for constructing confidence intervals for the parameters in empirical Bayes problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for constructing EB confidence intervals that are calibrated in the EB sense.

we propose an empirical Bayes (EM) method of interval estimation for a parameter of interest that is based on the posterior distribution of that parameter, but which accounts for the uncertainty in the estimation of hyperparameters of the prior.
the proposed EM intervals have good coverage and conditional calibration properties in finite samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EM interval is a viable alternative to the naive interval, especially in the case of small sample sizes.
EB intervals can be constructed that attain the desired coverage in the EB sense and are also calibrated.
EB intervals can be made to perform very well, and that this performance is not sensitive to the choice of prior.
